text:
monitoring-bot: ALERT: spawn-ecc-monitor reported spike in correctable ECC events on pool-gpu-us-west2. 25 GPUs crossed 100 CCEs in 10m window. Average Xid rises. https://grafana.redwood/internal/d/GPUs
Priya Rao: saw the alert, looking at pod evictions now. Is this transient (driver) or a hw trend?
Alex Chen: quick check: nvidia-smi -q -d ECC on affected nodes shows frequent 'Correctable ECC' increments. Xid 33/35/117 intermittently in dmesg.
Marco Diaz: past incidents: Xid 33 often correlates with thermal stress or power rail flakiness. But Xid flood + CCEs across many cards suggests a firmware/driver regression or a noisy batch workload.
Cindy Park: cluster capacity note: us-west2 is at 82% GPU utilization. If we start draining, we could saturate other regions. Need plan to avoid throttling latency SLOs for hosted API.
Priya Rao: proposal: create a graded auto-drain policy rather than immediate evict. Steps: 1) If a card reports >200 CCEs in 30m -> mark soft-drain (no new pods scheduled to that card). 2) If errors continue and Xid activity spikes to >50 in 1h -> hard-drain and replacement. 3) Always try safe reboot before RMA.
Alex Chen: +1. Add cooldown and cross-check with driver version: only auto-drain if driver >= 535.54 (we saw older drivers miscount). Also tag nodes with 'auto-drain-enabled' so Dedicated customers don't lose reserved capacity unexpectedly.
Marco Diaz: ops commands we used before:
```
# list cards with ECC counter
for n in $(cat nodes.txt); do ssh $n "nvidia-smi --query-gpu=index,ecc.errors.corrected.volatile --format=csv,noheader"; done
# check kernel logs
ssh node "dmesg | grep -i xid | tail -n 200"
```
Priya Rao: runbook snippet to add to infra playbooks channel:
```
If monitoring-bot alerts CCE spike:
- check per-card counters (nvidia-smi)
- check dmesg for Xid codes
- mark node soft-drain (cordon GPUs) and notify oncall
- if repeat after 60m -> escalate to vendor and start RMA cadence
```
ops-oncall: manual action taken: cordoned node node-usw2-14 at 1765002200, migrated 6 pods. No customer impact yet. Recorded in incident tracker: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INF-8672
Cindy Park: can we add capacity buffer rule? Suggest: keep 10% spare GPUs in each region or enable temporary cross-region burst for ML-hosted until replacement completes. Need cost approval for burst hours.
Alex Chen: auto-drain policy config proposal (fields):
```
- window_minutes: 30
- soft_drain_threshold: 200
- hard_drain_threshold: 500
- xid_escalation_count: 50
- cooldown_minutes: 120
- enabled_tags: ["auto-drain-enabled"]
- max_concurrent_drains_per_region: 3
```
Priya Rao: decision: enable soft-drain by default for infra nodes with tag auto-drain-enabled, set soft threshold 200/30m, cooldown 120m. Hard-drain requires manual approve from oncall if region spare capacity < 10%.
Marco Diaz: action items: Marco to draft a short automation PR to implement thresholds and tag filters; Alex to add driver-version gating; Cindy to open cost request for burst capacity and document region buffer policy.
ops-oncall: logged action owner notes: Marco (draft PR) due 1765080000, Alex (driver gate) due 1765065000, Cindy (cost request) due 1765090000. I'll keep the cordon in place until PR lands or RMA proceeds.
Priya Rao: thanks. I'll post the runbook update to #infra-playbooks and ping support-vendor with node dump attached. :thumbsup:
Alex Chen: adding a tiny script for safe cordon to the repo in the PR, sample:
```
#!/bin/bash
NODE=$1
kubectl annotate node $NODE gpu-drain=soft --overwrite
kubectl label node $NODE auto-drain-enabled=true --overwrite
# evict pods with pod disruption budget awareness
kubectl drain $NODE --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force --grace-period=120
```
monitoring-bot: NOTE: alert suppressed for node-usw2-14 after cordon at 1765002300.
Priya Rao: closing the thread for now — will escalate if numbers climb.
